title: Enhancing Al-Cu Alloys Produced by High-Energy Milling and Sintered by High Frequency Induction Heating for Microstructure Control
content: Mechanical alloying is an effective method for producing nanostructured materials, including metals, ceramics, and composites. High-energy ball milling (HEBM) has recently gained research interest due to its cost-effectiveness, despite its complexity [1], Nanostructured composites prepared by HEBM exhibit superior mechanical properties [2], but the resulting powders require a posterior sintering process. Conventional sintering methods involve high temperature and long holding time, affecting the material properties. Increased temperature enhances particle bonding and reduces porosity but also negatively alters its microstructure, leading to residual stress relaxation, grain growth, and phase transitions [3]. High-frequency induction heating, which is widely used for ceramic sintering, has recently gained attention in powder metallurgy for sintering metals processed by HEBM, achieving high densification in shorter times [4].
